blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes a comprehensive survey by Conti et al. on security and privacy issues in Bitcoin, focusing on a catalog of major attacks and their defenses. The post highlights several double-spending attacks (Finney, Brute Force, Vector 76) and their mechanics, emphasizing that miners with disproportionate hashrate power can significantly increase the risk of such attacks. The key insight is that while waiting for multiple confirmations (e.g., 6 blocks) is the most effective defense, fast-payment scenarios require alternative detection mechanisms. The survey also discusses the catastrophic 51% attack (Goldfinger attack), selfish mining, block withholding, and other misbehavior attacks, concluding that no complete protection exists and that these remain open challenges for researchers.
paper_title: A survey on security and privacy issues of Bitcoin
